This is no guide. Just my thoughts and stuff I had to deal with when convincing my gf to go linux instead of windows.

Laptop: too drunk to get model. will edit tomorrow

Needed apps: Internet browser, popcorn-time, spotify, TOUCH SCREEN SCROLLING

Still struggling with: USB Realtek wifi not waking up after sleep. Have to replug.

My own needed stuff: Steam, FTL, Kerbal space.

First I showed her Mint 17 from USB. She was not satisfied with the interface. I installed Ubuntu 14.04 lTS with Gnome3 instead of unity. Touch screen scrolling was not working in Chrome or Firefox. Chromium solved that. Touch scrolling works by default in Chromium. Also, in settings you can enable "Use system titles and borders" to remove the title bar. Gnome3 is an OK replacement for Win8. She likes it. The interface is kind of touch friendly and sleek/modern.

After some tweaking, Ubuntu 14.04 was working fine. Even steam games. Only one problem. The USB wifi adapter would not wake up after sleep/suspend. I thought Upgrading to 15.04 would help. Mistake.

Ubuntu 15.04 did not solve the USB wifi problem. And in 15.04 I had graphic and sound stuttering in steam games. Every 5 seconds the FPS would drop to 0. I could not even play FTL. I wanted to keep 15.04 since 15.10 is released soon.. I tried installing the latest Kernel. No luck. Games are stuttering. Every 5 seconds the mouse icon dissappears and the game freezes for a second or two. I started over and installed 14.10 which has support for the intel graphics driver tool. All is good now, except the USB wifi problem.

Well there you go. Im going to sleep now.
My experience installing Linux in a touchscreen laptop

OK I didnt sleep just yet. Installed Intel Graphics drivers on Ubuntu 14.10:

How I did it:

https://01.org/linuxgraphics/downloads download: "Graphics Installer 1.1.0 for Ubuntu* 14.10, 64-bit" --- link https://download.01.org/gfx/ubuntu/14.10/main/pool/main/i/intel-linux-graphics-installer/intel-linux-graphics-installer_1.1.0-0intel1_amd64.deb

This will install about 26 packages. Reboot and the intel graphics driver works very nicely. Kerbal space program runs on low graphics without lag or stuttering,

Edit: Games are working very nicely with the latest Intel Graphics driver for Ubuntu (gnome) 14.10.

Touch scrolling seems to be application-specific. Works in Chromium and popcorn time so far. Spotify for linux does not have touch scrolling, Steam for linux does'nt either.

I will try Spotify in Wine but I doubt touch scrolling will work.

OBS: Touch is working in all apps. Pressing the scroll and dragging works.
14.10 is working really well on this Intel graphics laptop. I'm running Chromium, Mad Max in popcorn time, music in spotify and kerbal in steam with no lag.
